releaseApproval.reviewer: User-authorized v2.0.5 server-shared wallpaper release; additive SQLite schema and unchanged encrypted user-data formats reviewed
evidence: The wallpaper is a single bounded (10 MiB) plaintext system asset in SQLite schema 8. Its read endpoint is intentionally unauthenticated so the login page can display it; upload and deletion require a valid session, CSRF token and same-origin request. The asset is backed up with SQLite and is excluded from encrypted user-file quota.

The encrypted object envelope, vault/key-slot formats, encrypted file metadata, AAD, browser recovery payloads, client mutation protocol, and backup container format are unchanged. Backup restore accepts snapshot schemas 2–8.
This release also updates the brand mark/favicon and adds the live transfer-speed indicator. The prior v2.0.4 video startup and diagnostics behavior is retained.

Full local make test passed on 2026-10-12: web typecheck/lint/build, Go vet and tests, installer/upgrade/uninstall checks, release-format and persistent-format contracts, 560 frontend tests, and 3 TLS proxy tests. Existing lint warnings remain; no release check failed.
Publication requires full local make test, exact-commit main CI with all-package race tests and Linux amd64/arm64 builds, followed by released archive checksum verification.

scope: XDrive v2.0.5 adds a server-shared, publicly readable plaintext desktop wallpaper for login and desktop screens, backed by additive SQLite schema 8; encrypted user-data formats remain unchanged

meaning.1: legacy direct Vault Key file and thumbnail derivation
meaning.2: K_data hierarchy for newly encrypted files and thumbnails

localState.plaintextPolicy: encrypted with K_local before IndexedDB persistence

sqlite.migrationPolicy: forward only; after a schema-changing migration, restore the matching pre-migration database and binary before rollback

clientMutationProtocol.acceptance: exact match only; reject missing, older, and future versions before reading mutation bodies

evolutionPolicy: Unknown payload versions and unknown fields remain fail-closed.
The listed optional fields and their absent-value meanings are part of the current schema contract.
Adding or redefining a payload field requires a new payload schema version; it must not silently expand an older strict reader.
A change that makes a stale client unsafe for mutations increments the client mutation protocol version in Go and TypeScript.
Key derivation or AAD meaning changes use their own crypto version; they do not reuse a payload schema number.
SQLite schema migration, backup container format, encrypted object envelope, and browser payload schema are independent version dimensions.
